questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a high-ranking university located in a nice city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I remember it as being pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro day where we got all the information we needed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got an email from KU about the possibility to live at the Danish YWCA in London. Probably wouldn't have found it if KU hadn't informed me

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In London, it's cheaper option to stay at the YWCA and there's a fantastic community on top of that

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If it's the housing provided by the university that is being asked about, I can't say since I didn't live in student housing

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was helped by my friend who had been an exchange student at King's College before, otherwise I think it might have been more difficult to register for courses. There were many different websites and forms, which were a bit difficult to navigate. They did provide a guide for the course registration, but the system was quite complex nevertheless

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much. And it was very difficult to find out who to contact about questions for the course registration

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up doing it right and getting the courses I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't do it last minute. Or befriend one who has already studied at King's College

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was adequate

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was not much different than what I'm used to at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global Politics, The Political Economy of the EU, Britain and Europe Since 1945, Anglo-American Relations Since 1945

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was very happy to attend the two history courses Britain and Europe Since 1945, Anglo-American Relations Since 1945. I would definitely recommend taking advantage of the opportunity to take courses at different departments

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many sports clubs and societies available. I tried signing up for the tennis club, but the window for registration was so short that I didn't make it, and I was told that it would be possible to sign up later, which turned out not to be true. It seemed to be the same for all the sports clubs, so I would recommend future students to sign up as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a couple of societies, like the Nordic Society and the Conservative Society, which hosted different events that I attended a few off. But I also joined other societies that never seemed to host anything and it was very scarce with information, so that was a bit disappointing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on day trips around the country. You can catch a train to almost anywhere from London. But it's expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a society

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much. Brits are however very polite and therefore indirect, which can be a bit difficult for Danes who are usually more direct about things

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Good sense of humour

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you're going as a MA student, lower your expectations regarding socialising because that seems to be easier as a BA student. Not that it's impossible to get friends at uni, but you should not put all of your eggs in that one basket - try seeking out other places too for meeting new people

Look at the exam form when choosing courses. Many courses include participation in classes as part of the mark along with several exam forms like a presentation, briefing paper, and oral exam. So don't choose those.

Save up a lot of money because London is expensive

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nope

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting the opportunity to take two history courses and dive into completely different subjects that I wasn't used to from political science. I learned a lot from that. 

And staying at the YWCA was a great decision as I made a lot of new friends there, although I didn't get a lot of local friends, but as I said that appeared to be quite difficult too.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Writing four exams alone when you're used to making group exams back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
